title: Diabetes, hypertension and CKD together
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, kidney disease and any related hypertension and dialysis status.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for CKD and hypertension.

HPI
Pt is a 61-year-old male presenting for routine follow-up of chronic kidney disease and hypertension. Pt reports feeling well overall today. He currently manages his type 2 diabetes through diet and exercise alone. No reports of acute changes in renal function or blood pressure.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Amlodipine 5mg daily
Multivitamin daily

Exam
BP: 132/82. HR: 72, RRR. CTAB. WNL. Pt alert and oriented x3. No acute distress.

Assessment
1. Chronic kidney disease, stage 4. Recent eGFR is 22 mL/min/1.73m2.
2. Hypertension. BP stable on current regimen.
3. Type 2 diabetes. Managed via diet.

Plan
Continue current medications. Monitor renal function and electrolytes. Follow up in 3 months.

Electronically signed, K. Nguyen, DO, 05/12/2026
explanations: Type 2 diabetes and CKD are linked by the 'with' convention unless the provider says otherwise: E11.22 (HCC 37).
Hypertension with CKD stage 1-4 is presumed linked: I12.9. Both links apply at once: diabetes with CKD and hypertensive CKD.
The CKD stage is coded in addition: N18.4.

distractors.why: The 'with' convention presumes the diabetes caused the CKD.
Hypertension and CKD are presumed linked: I12.-, not I10.
I12.0 is for stage 5 or ESRD only.
E11.22 says to use an additional code for the CKD stage.
